diagram_math_checks.justification: For any unit v in R^n, y=x+zv has |y-x|=|z|. Definition (ii) therefore intersects the spatial closed ball with this line in the closed interval |z|<=rho_n(tau). Caption explicitly identifies this one-dimensional section and the n-dimensional full slice; no sphere in R^(n+1) is asserted.

Set A=r^2/(4pi), u=tau/A. The source radius satisfies rho_n(Au)^2=(2nA)u log(1/u), while rho_max^2=2nA/e by (iii). Plotted horizontal coordinates are +/-1.6 sqrt(e u log(1/u)) and vertical coordinates 4(1-u); hence upward means increasing s=t-Au. Numerical samples include u=0 and 1 as zero-width endpoints, u=1/e as widest, and u=.7 as the solid slice. Independent horizontal/vertical scales are declared.

Local compactness/enclosure Remark differentiates u log(1/u), yielding maximum at u=1/e. Figure width is +/-1.6 and height 4(1-1/e)=2.528482..., matching drawn 2.5285 and label s=t-r^2/(4pi e). Solid slice at u=.7 has height 1.2 and half-width 1.3181, matching the outline samples and illustrating an interior depth tau.

Definition explicitly adjoins (x,t), while clause (ii) states the singleton {x} at tau=A and no points at tau>A. Both endpoint marks are therefore filled, at figure heights 4 and 0; the lower label s=t-r^2/(4pi) and empty-below caption agree. No open endpoint is intended.

All original definition/Remarks arguments remain exact. Figure claims follow from (ii), (iii) and the existing radius derivation, and are never used as proof premises. Two explicit sampled polylines each start at (0,4) and finish at (0,0); they visibly meet at both filled points. No named-node cycle or missing closing edge is involved.
